messages:
sec-alert-bot: [ALERT] SSO impossible-travel detected for user jdoe@redwood.com. Sessions observed from IPs 3.122.45.10 (eu-west-1) and 34.56.78.90 (us-east-1) within 12m. Device fingerprint mismatch. Alert ID SSO-2567. Auto-risk score: HIGH. Please investigate.
maria: picking this up. user is Julian Doe (eng). I'll check Okta sessions and active tokens.
aj: oncall here. Maria, +1. Can we immediately revoke all sessions and force reauth? If suspicious, also rotate any active API tokens for that user.
josh: I'm running an Okta session revoke now. Command: `okta sessions close --user 00u1ABCdef --all`. Also checking MFA logs.
kyle: checking audit logs for KMS access and vault tokens used by that user — `vault token-lookup -accessor abc123` and `gcloud kms keys versions list`.
sarah: If confirmed compromise, I'll prepare a short internal note and customer-facing stub. Prefer to avoid external notification unless we see data exfil.
maria: Revoked both sessions via Okta. Also observed 4 failed password attempts from 3 distinct EU IPs prior to second login attempt. Looks like MFA push fatigue — user accepted one push?
aj: Did user report any unusual prompts? Reach out to Julian via phone, not slack/email.
maria: pinged on his mobile. He says he received multiple MFA pushes and clicked allow because of noise. He doesn't recognize the IPs.
josh: we've rotated the user's API keys and disabled all long-lived tokens. Also invalidated OAuth grants.
kyle: KMS access audit: no `crypto.decrypt` calls by that principal in last 48h. Looks like no key material touched.
ops-bot: automation: created incident INC-2026-194 in PagerDuty, priority P2.
sarah: drafting internal post: include timeline, actions (revoked sessions, rotated keys, user outreach), recommended follow-ups: mandatory MFA hard-factors, evaluate push-notification fatigue.
aj: next steps: 1) check other accounts for similar pattern (same IPs), 2) add rate-limits to push auth, 3) temporary disable push-only MFA option for org.
maria: running search across Okta logs for IPs 3.122.45.10 and 34.56.78.90. Found 7 attempts across 3 users in last hour.
josh: I recommend we force re-enrollment to TOTP or WebAuthn for flagged users and enable 'deny if impossible-travel' global rule until investigation done.
kyle: also recommend KMS key rotation schedule note in follow-up, but not immediate as no access detected.
sarah: publishing internal note now. I'll add a 'what to tell customers' short line: no evidence of data access; impacted only session tokens; user credentials being rotated.
aj: closing loop: create a post-incident task list and schedule a retro with Sec+IR tomorrow 10am.
maria: adding evidence: exporting Okta logs to S3: s3://redwood-sec/INC-2026-194/okta-logs.json
ops-bot: automation: added runbook tag 'sso-impossible-travel' to incident.
josh: put a hold on self-serve SSO session extension feature for 24h in case of chaining.
maria: confirmed Julian's machine scanned, no malware detected.
aj: thanks everyone. If new indicators, re-open channel and escalate to P1.
